Purpose

The `ast` package (`ast` and subpackages) models the fuzzy rule block of a function block as an immutable tree of typed nodes. The parser builds the tree while reducing the `RULEBLOCK` grammar rules, through `parser.facades.RuleblockASTBuilder`, which maps the `parser.tree.TreeNode` built during the reductions into `ast` nodes. The resulting `ast.AbstractSyntaxTree` is the input of the lowering phase, which turns it into the rule matrix of the code generator.

Every node extends `ast.AbstractAstNode` and answers with a semantic label, such as `ROOT`, `IF`, `WITH`, `IS`, `NOT`, `AND`, `OR`, `BODY`, `ACTIVATION`, `ACCUMULATION`, or `COMPONENT`, or with the name of the rule block it represents. Nodes hold their attributes in final fields and their children in an unmodifiable list.

## Logical Operators

### Operator

`ast.ruleblock.operators.Operator` is the enum of logical operators: `ASUM`, `BDIF`, `BSUM`, `MAX`, `MIN`, `NSUM`, and `PROD`.

### OperatorNode

`ast.ruleblock.operators.OperatorNode` extends `ast.AbstractAstNode` and holds a logical operator together with its operands; its label is the operator name.

### OperatorFactory

`ast.ruleblock.operators.OperatorFactory` is a final utility class with static default operators: `orDefault` returns `MAX`, `andDefault` returns `MIN`, `actDefault` returns `MIN`, and `accuDefault` returns `MAX`.

## Construction from the Parser

The `parser.Parser` assigns the AST after reducing the `rule_block` rule: the generated parser accumulates `RuleBlockNode` instances into a list and wraps them into an `ast.AbstractSyntaxTree`.

sections.Lowering:
`lowering.RuleLowering.lower(ast.AbstractSyntaxTree)` returns the rows of the supported rules: one row per rule, one column per input and then per output, each cell holding the index of the term of that variable.

`lowering.ControllerLowering.lower(ast.AbstractSyntaxTree)` builds the `codegen.ControllerModel` from the AST and the symbol table. The model is built only if the program follows the Basic Level subset: exactly one rule block, accumulation `ACCU: MAX`, each rule an `AND: MIN` of `input IS term` propositions that uses every input once and concludes `output IS term` for every output, and no weighting factor other than one.

Every problem is reported through `utils.DiagnosticsHandler` as an `utils.diagnostics.UnsupportedFeature` or an `utils.diagnostics.UndeclaredReference`.

Purpose

The codegen package (`codegen` and subpackages) consumes the immutable `codegen.ControllerModel` built by the lowering phase and emits the C++ source of a fuzzy controller for Vivado HLS:

* `<base>_out.cpp` — implementation of the fuzzy controller
* `<base>_out.h` — header with types and signatures
* `<base>_outTB.cpp` — test bench

The generator is a port of the code generator of Luca Sarramone (Generador-FLC, commit `c304c1d`), used with permission. The generated code is the same; the differences are internal: the model is passed explicitly instead of living in static fields, and the code is returned as text instead of being written to files.

## Controller Model

`codegen.ControllerModel` is the immutable input of the generator. It carries the bit width `N` of every value (`MIN_BIT_WIDTH = 1` to `MAX_BIT_WIDTH = 30`), the ordered input and output variables, the evaluation method that owns the rule matrix, and the defuzzifier of every output. The constructor validates the bit width, requires at least one input and one output, and requires every output to have a defuzzifier.

The maximum degree of the converter is `converterRange = 2^N - 1`, and every value of the controller is an unsigned integer of `N` bits (`ap_uint<N>`).

## Generated C++ Types

The generated controller uses the fixed point types:

* `fixed_int`: input value or membership degree, `ap_uint<N>`.
* `fixed_aux_<output>`: centroid accumulator of an output, `ap_uint<2N + number of sets>`.
* `fixed_out`: packed controller result, `ap_uint<N * number of outputs>`.

The test bench keeps the fixed types of the original generator: `fixed_int = ap_uint<8>` and `fixed_aux = ap_uint<18>`.

## Generation Stages

### Fuzzification Stage

`codegen.Fuzzifier` emits, for every input variable, the slope constants `function<var><i>`, the zero-initialized buffer `<var>Fuzz[n]`, and the `fuzzifier` function. The function applies `#pragma HLS PIPELINE` and `#pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION`, then evaluates every fuzzy set through `codegen.Variable.compile` into `<var>Fuzz[setNumber]`.

### Rule Evaluation Stage

`codegen.evaluation.EvaluationMethod` owns the rule matrix as an immutable list of rows, one row per rule and one cell per variable column. The column layout is the order of the inputs of the controller signature followed by the order of the packed outputs. `codegen.evaluation.MinMaxMethod` implements the AND as the minimum of the input membership degrees and the ACCUMULATION as the maximum over the rules that conclude the output set.

### Defuzzification Stage

`codegen.defuzzification.Defuzzifier` emits the `<output>MembershipValues[n]` buffers filled by the rule evaluation, and one defuzzifier function per output. `codegen.defuzzification.CentroidDefuzzifier` implements the centroid of the singleton output values (FCL `METHOD: CoGS`); when no rule fires, the denominator is zero.

## Generated Controller

`codegen.CodeGenerator.generateCpp` emits the implementation with the types, the slopes, the fuzzifier, the rule evaluation, the defuzzifiers, and the `fuzzyController` function annotated with `#pragma HLS DATAFLOW`. The controller returns the packed result of all outputs.

sections.Controller Model:
`codegen.ControllerModel` is the immutable input of the generator. It carries the bit width `N` of every value (`MIN_BIT_WIDTH = 1` to `MAX_BIT_WIDTH = 30`), the ordered input and output variables, the evaluation method that owns the rule matrix, and the defuzzifier of every output. The constructor validates the bit width, requires at least one input and one output, and requires every output to have a defuzzifier.

The maximum degree of the converter is `converterRange = 2^N - 1`, and every value of the controller is an unsigned integer of `N` bits (`ap_uint<N>`).
sections.Generated C++ Types:
The generated controller uses the fixed point types:

* `fixed_int`: input value or membership degree, `ap_uint<N>`.
* `fixed_aux_<output>`: centroid accumulator of an output, `ap_uint<2N + number of sets>`.
* `fixed_out`: packed controller result, `ap_uint<N * number of outputs>`.

The test bench keeps the fixed types of the original generator: `fixed_int = ap_uint<8>` and `fixed_aux = ap_uint<18>`.
sections.Fuzzification Stage: `codegen.Fuzzifier` emits, for every input variable, the slope constants `function<var><i>`, the zero-initialized buffer `<var>Fuzz[n]`, and the `fuzzifier` function. The function applies `#pragma HLS PIPELINE` and `#pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION`, then evaluates every fuzzy set through `codegen.Variable.compile` into `<var>Fuzz[setNumber]`.
sections.Rule Evaluation Stage: `codegen.evaluation.EvaluationMethod` owns the rule matrix as an immutable list of rows, one row per rule and one cell per variable column. The column layout is the order of the inputs of the controller signature followed by the order of the packed outputs. `codegen.evaluation.MinMaxMethod` implements the AND as the minimum of the input membership degrees and the ACCUMULATION as the maximum over the rules that conclude the output set.
sections.Defuzzification Stage: `codegen.defuzzification.Defuzzifier` emits the `<output>MembershipValues[n]` buffers filled by the rule evaluation, and one defuzzifier function per output. `codegen.defuzzification.CentroidDefuzzifier` implements the centroid of the singleton output values (FCL `METHOD: CoGS`); when no rule fires, the denominator is zero.
sections.Generated Controller: `codegen.CodeGenerator.generateCpp` emits the implementation with the types, the slopes, the fuzzifier, the rule evaluation, the defuzzifiers, and the `fuzzyController` function annotated with `#pragma HLS DATAFLOW`. The controller returns the packed result of all outputs.

## Architecture Overview

The parser follows a Publisher + Director + Builder architecture. The Bison-generated `Parser` reduces grammar rules and, in semantic actions, builds `Publisher` instances, configures them through `Director` recipes and `LexemeInfoBuilder`, then calls `publish()` to write into `utils.SymbolTable`. Mangling (`FB#varName` for scoped variables, `TypeName` for types) is inline in Publisher implementations and `IdentifierParser`; there is no separate NameMangler class.

```
                 Parser.y semantic action
                        |
                        v
                 +-------------+
                 |   Director  |  makeWithMetadata / makeDefaultXxx recipes
                 +-------------+
                        |
                        v (configures)
                 +-------------+
                 | LexemeInfo  |  fluent build of semantic attributes
                 |   Builder   |
                 +-------------+
                        |
                        v (passed to)
                 +-------------+        publish()        +--------------+
                 |  Publisher  | ----------------------> | SymbolTable  |
                 | (Declaration|        keys()           | (LexemeInfo) |
                 |  / Multiple)|                          +--------------+
                 +-------------+
                        |
                        v (inline mangling scope#name)
                 SymbolTable keys e.g. MAIN#X, MAIN#Y
```

## Key Components

### LexemeInfoMutator

`utils.builders.LexemeInfoMutator` is the fluent interface for setting semantic attributes on a lexeme: `type`, `subtype`, `customType`, `source`, `use`, `inferiorLimits`, `superiorLimits`, `parameters`, `initialValue`. Every setter returns the mutator for chaining. `parser.publishers.Publisher` extends this interface, so publishers can be configured with the same fluent API before publishing.

### LexemeInfoBuilder

`utils.builders.LexemeInfoBuilder` implements both `LexemeInfoMutator` and `LexemeInfoView`. It holds the mutable attributes (`type`, `subtype`, `customType`, `use`, `source`, `inferiorLimit`, `superiorLimit`, `parameters`, `initialValue`) and `build()` produces an immutable `utils.LexemeInfo`. Used by `Declaration` and directly in semantic actions (e.g. linguistic terms).

### Director

`utils.builders.Director` is a static utility providing predefined recipes:

| Recipe                         | Effect                                                               |
|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| makeWithMetadata(schema, view) | Copies all attributes from a LexemeInfoView into a LexemeInfoMutator |
| makeLiteral(schema)            | Sets type=SIMPLE, use=LITERAL, source=NONE                           |
| makeDefaultInteger(schema)     | Returns "0"; subtype INT, initialValue 0                             |
| makeDefaultReal(schema)        | Returns "0.0"; subtype REAL, initialValue 0.0                        |
| makeDefaultBoolean(schema)     | Returns "FALSE"; subtype BOOL, initialValue false                    |
| makeTrueBoolean(schema)        | Returns "TRUE"; subtype BOOL, initialValue true                      |
| makeDefaultString(schema)      | Returns "''"; subtype STRING, initialValue ""                        |
| makeDefaultWString(schema)     | Returns '""'; subtype WSTRING, initialValue ""                       |

These recipes guarantee consistent literal/default registration across semantic actions.

### Publisher Hierarchy

`parser.publishers.Publisher` (interface) declares `setDeclarationScope(String)`, `publish()`, and `List<String> keys()`. It extends `LexemeInfoMutator`.

```
Publisher (interface)
├── Declaration (abstract)  -- holds LexemeInfoBuilder
│   ├── MultipleDeclaration  -- many identifiers, same attributes
│   ├── SingleDeclaration    -- one identifier, key scope#name
│   │   ├── ComponentDeclaration  -- fuzzifier/defuzzifier + terms
│   │   ├── StructureDeclaration  -- struct + field block
│   │   ├── EnumeratedTypeDeclaration -- enum + macro registration
│   │   └── AnnonymousEnumeratedField -- anonymous enum field + macros
│   └── DeclarationGroup (composite)
│       ├── DeclarationBlock  -- IO variable declarations
│       ├── StructureBlock    -- struct fields + init info
│       └── TermBlock         -- linguistic terms
└── MultipleDeclaration
    └── AnnonymousEnumeratedVariable -- anonymous enum variable + macros
```

Keys are mangled inline: scoped variables use `FB#varName`, types use `TypeName`. Example: `x, y : INT` in block `MAIN` publishes as `MAIN#X`, `MAIN#Y`.

### Factory and Initialization Hierarchy

`parser.initializations.Factory.createPrimitiveInitialization(SymbolTable, Subtype)` returns a `DefaultInitialization` and supports BOOL, REAL/LREAL, STRING, WSTRING, and all integer subtypes SINT through ULINT (throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise).

```
Initialization (interface: find, variableValue, copy)
├── LeafInitialization (abstract; find only empty path)
│   ├── DefaultInitialization   -- BOOL / INT / REAL / STRING / WSTRING default
│   ├── VariableInitialization  -- reference to another variable
│   ├── EnumeratedInitialization -- selected enum literal
│   ├── SubrangeInitialization  -- lower bound of subrange
│   └── MacroInitialization     -- enum ordinal, registered as INT literal
└── NodeInitialization (abstract; put / find over paths)
    ├── StructInitialization    -- named fields, nested # paths
    └── RepeatedInitialization  -- array over disjoint intervals
```

Path syntax uses `#` as separator (e.g. `RGB#R`, `2#X`, `0..3#field`).

| Block                 | Tokens                                   | Purpose                                   |
|-----------------------|------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Function block        | FUNCTION_BLOCK ... END_FUNCTION_BLOCK    | Top-level program unit with name and body |
| Fuzzify               | FUZZIFY ... END_FUZZIFY                  | Linguistic fuzzifier component            |
| Defuzzify             | DEFUZZIFY ... END_DEFUZZIFY              | Linguistic defuzzifier component          |
| Rule block            | RULEBLOCK ... END_RULEBLOCK              | Fuzzy rule with operators and activation  |
| Option                | OPTION ... END_OPTION                    | Manufacturer-specific pragmas             |
| Variable declarations | VAR / VAR_INPUT / VAR_OUTPUT ... END_VAR | Declared variables with scope             |

### Fuzzify / Defuzzify

Fuzzify blocks declare linguistic terms (`TERM name := value;` or membership functions) and are published as components with source FUZZIFY. Defuzzify blocks add an optional `RANGE ( lo .. hi );`, a default value, and a defuzzification method (COG, COGS, COA, LM, RM) and are published with source DEFUZZIFY. Both register term names as parameters.

### Rule Block

A rule block declares OR/AND operators, an activation method, an accumulation method, and rules (`IF condition WITH body`). The parser builds a `TreeNode` via `ConditionParsingContext` and converts it to a `RuleBlockNode` AST using `RuleblockASTBuilder` with an operator configuration list.

### Variable Declarations Annex B

Variables are declared under `VAR`, `VAR_INPUT`, or `VAR_OUTPUT` with optional RETAIN/NON_RETAIN retain spec and an initialization list. Each `DeclarationBlock` is configured with source (IN/OUT), use VARIABLE, declaration scope (function block name), then published. Keys are `scope#identifier`.

### Data Types

Elementary types: BOOL, SINT/INT/DINT/LINT, USINT/UINT/UDINT/ULINT, REAL/LREAL, STRING, WSTRING, TIME, DATE, DATE_AND_TIME, TIME_OF_DAY, BYTE/WORD/DWORD/LWORD, plus bit-string and date types. User-defined types: enumerated, subrange, array, structure.

### Initializations

Initialization grammar covers simple spec (numeric/string/boolean constant), boolean spec (edge), custom spec (constant/identifier/structure), enumerated spec, array spec (with repeated initial elements), structure spec (field inits), string spec, and standard function block spec.

### Data Type Declaration

`TYPE ... END_TYPE` encloses a list of type declarations (`type_name_declaration`), each with a type specification (structure, enumerated, subrange, array, string).

sections.Architecture Overview:
The parser follows a Publisher + Director + Builder architecture. The Bison-generated `Parser` reduces grammar rules and, in semantic actions, builds `Publisher` instances, configures them through `Director` recipes and `LexemeInfoBuilder`, then calls `publish()` to write into `utils.SymbolTable`. Mangling (`FB#varName` for scoped variables, `TypeName` for types) is inline in Publisher implementations and `IdentifierParser`; there is no separate NameMangler class.

```
                 Parser.y semantic action
                        |
                        v
                 +-------------+
                 |   Director  |  makeWithMetadata / makeDefaultXxx recipes
                 +-------------+
                        |
                        v (configures)
                 +-------------+
                 | LexemeInfo  |  fluent build of semantic attributes
                 |   Builder   |
                 +-------------+
                        |
                        v (passed to)
                 +-------------+        publish()        +--------------+
                 |  Publisher  | ----------------------> | SymbolTable  |
                 | (Declaration|        keys()           | (LexemeInfo) |
                 |  / Multiple)|                          +--------------+
                 +-------------+
                        |
                        v (inline mangling scope#name)
                 SymbolTable keys e.g. MAIN#X, MAIN#Y
```
sections.LexemeInfoMutator: `utils.builders.LexemeInfoMutator` is the fluent interface for setting semantic attributes on a lexeme: `type`, `subtype`, `customType`, `source`, `use`, `inferiorLimits`, `superiorLimits`, `parameters`, `initialValue`. Every setter returns the mutator for chaining. `parser.publishers.Publisher` extends this interface, so publishers can be configured with the same fluent API before publishing.
sections.LexemeInfoBuilder: `utils.builders.LexemeInfoBuilder` implements both `LexemeInfoMutator` and `LexemeInfoView`. It holds the mutable attributes (`type`, `subtype`, `customType`, `use`, `source`, `inferiorLimit`, `superiorLimit`, `parameters`, `initialValue`) and `build()` produces an immutable `utils.LexemeInfo`. Used by `Declaration` and directly in semantic actions (e.g. linguistic terms).
sections.Director:
`utils.builders.Director` is a static utility providing predefined recipes:

| Recipe                         | Effect                                                               |
|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| makeWithMetadata(schema, view) | Copies all attributes from a LexemeInfoView into a LexemeInfoMutator |
| makeLiteral(schema)            | Sets type=SIMPLE, use=LITERAL, source=NONE                           |
| makeDefaultInteger(schema)     | Returns "0"; subtype INT, initialValue 0                             |
| makeDefaultReal(schema)        | Returns "0.0"; subtype REAL, initialValue 0.0                        |
| makeDefaultBoolean(schema)     | Returns "FALSE"; subtype BOOL, initialValue false                    |
| makeTrueBoolean(schema)        | Returns "TRUE"; subtype BOOL, initialValue true                      |
| makeDefaultString(schema)      | Returns "''"; subtype STRING, initialValue ""                        |
| makeDefaultWString(schema)     | Returns '""'; subtype WSTRING, initialValue ""                       |

These recipes guarantee consistent literal/default registration across semantic actions.
sections.Publisher Hierarchy:
`parser.publishers.Publisher` (interface) declares `setDeclarationScope(String)`, `publish()`, and `List<String> keys()`. It extends `LexemeInfoMutator`.

```
Publisher (interface)
├── Declaration (abstract)  -- holds LexemeInfoBuilder
│   ├── MultipleDeclaration  -- many identifiers, same attributes
│   ├── SingleDeclaration    -- one identifier, key scope#name
│   │   ├── ComponentDeclaration  -- fuzzifier/defuzzifier + terms
│   │   ├── StructureDeclaration  -- struct + field block
│   │   ├── EnumeratedTypeDeclaration -- enum + macro registration
│   │   └── AnnonymousEnumeratedField -- anonymous enum field + macros
│   └── DeclarationGroup (composite)
│       ├── DeclarationBlock  -- IO variable declarations
│       ├── StructureBlock    -- struct fields + init info
│       └── TermBlock         -- linguistic terms
└── MultipleDeclaration
    └── AnnonymousEnumeratedVariable -- anonymous enum variable + macros
```

Keys are mangled inline: scoped variables use `FB#varName`, types use `TypeName`. Example: `x, y : INT` in block `MAIN` publishes as `MAIN#X`, `MAIN#Y`.
sections.Factory and Initialization Hierarchy:
`parser.initializations.Factory.createPrimitiveInitialization(SymbolTable, Subtype)` returns a `DefaultInitialization` and supports BOOL, REAL/LREAL, STRING, WSTRING, and all integer subtypes SINT through ULINT (throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise).

```
Initialization (interface: find, variableValue, copy)
├── LeafInitialization (abstract; find only empty path)
│   ├── DefaultInitialization   -- BOOL / INT / REAL / STRING / WSTRING default
│   ├── VariableInitialization  -- reference to another variable
│   ├── EnumeratedInitialization -- selected enum literal
│   ├── SubrangeInitialization  -- lower bound of subrange
│   └── MacroInitialization     -- enum ordinal, registered as INT literal
└── NodeInitialization (abstract; put / find over paths)
    ├── StructInitialization    -- named fields, nested # paths
    └── RepeatedInitialization  -- array over disjoint intervals
```

Path syntax uses `#` as separator (e.g. `RGB#R`, `2#X`, `0..3#field`).

mermaid_diagrams.title:
Results and Errors

* `SemanticAnalyzer.LexicalContext` carries `preprocessedLexeme`, line, `SymbolTable`, and `DiagnosticsHandler`; `SemanticAnalyzer.Result` carries **`lexeme`** and **`token`**, in that order in the constructor. `processAndSaveYylval` saves `result.lexeme` in `yylval` and returns `result.token`. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/SemanticAnalyzer.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/Lexer.flex`.
* `NumbersAnalyzer` returns `NUMERIC_LITERAL`; when the subtype is `UNKNOWN`, it logs a warning and stores the recovery `ParsedValue`, whose key may differ from the original lexeme. `Naturals`, `Integers`, `Reals`, and base analyzers provide their respective recoveries. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/NumbersAnalyzer.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/Naturals.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/Integers.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/Reals.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/bases/BaseNumbersAnalyzer.java`.
* `Dates`, `DayTimes`, and `DateAndDayTimes` store `LocalDate`, `LocalTime`, and `LocalDateTime`; `Intervals` stores `Duration` and verifies limits of subordinate magnitudes and accumulated nanoseconds. In their error paths, a diagnostic is added and `YYerror` is returned. The temporal actions of `Lexer.flex` only return `TIME_LITERAL` if there is no `YYerror`; otherwise, they reset the state and continue scanning. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/Dates.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/DayTimes.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/DateAndDayTimes.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/Intervals.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/Lexer.flex`.
* `StringsAnalyzer` applies **`MAX_STRING_LENGTH = 255` to STRING and WSTRING** alike, measures Java's `content.length()` after resolving escapes, truncates content and key, issues `StringLengthWarning`, and returns `STRING_LITERAL`. Hexadecimal escapes are interpreted via `StringHexResolver` with two digits and `WStringHexResolver` with four. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/strings/StringsAnalyzer.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/strings/Strings.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/strings/WStrings.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/transformers/hex_resolvers/StringHexResolver.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/transformers/hex_resolvers/WStringHexResolver.java`.
* `Identifiers` returns the direct token for a reserved word other than `TRUE` or `FALSE`; for booleans it registers `Subtype.BOOL` and returns `BOOLEAN_LITERAL`; for identifiers it registers initial metadata and returns `IDENTIFIER`. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/Identifiers.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/utils/ReservedWords.java`.

sections.Results and Errors:
* `SemanticAnalyzer.LexicalContext` carries `preprocessedLexeme`, line, `SymbolTable`, and `DiagnosticsHandler`; `SemanticAnalyzer.Result` carries **`lexeme`** and **`token`**, in that order in the constructor. `processAndSaveYylval` saves `result.lexeme` in `yylval` and returns `result.token`. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/SemanticAnalyzer.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/Lexer.flex`.
* `NumbersAnalyzer` returns `NUMERIC_LITERAL`; when the subtype is `UNKNOWN`, it logs a warning and stores the recovery `ParsedValue`, whose key may differ from the original lexeme. `Naturals`, `Integers`, `Reals`, and base analyzers provide their respective recoveries. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/NumbersAnalyzer.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/Naturals.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/Integers.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/Reals.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/numbers/bases/BaseNumbersAnalyzer.java`.
* `Dates`, `DayTimes`, and `DateAndDayTimes` store `LocalDate`, `LocalTime`, and `LocalDateTime`; `Intervals` stores `Duration` and verifies limits of subordinate magnitudes and accumulated nanoseconds. In their error paths, a diagnostic is added and `YYerror` is returned. The temporal actions of `Lexer.flex` only return `TIME_LITERAL` if there is no `YYerror`; otherwise, they reset the state and continue scanning. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/Dates.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/DayTimes.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/DateAndDayTimes.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/Intervals.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/Lexer.flex`.
* `StringsAnalyzer` applies **`MAX_STRING_LENGTH = 255` to STRING and WSTRING** alike, measures Java's `content.length()` after resolving escapes, truncates content and key, issues `StringLengthWarning`, and returns `STRING_LITERAL`. Hexadecimal escapes are interpreted via `StringHexResolver` with two digits and `WStringHexResolver` with four. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/strings/StringsAnalyzer.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/strings/Strings.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/strings/WStrings.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/transformers/hex_resolvers/StringHexResolver.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/transformers/hex_resolvers/WStringHexResolver.java`.
* `Identifiers` returns the direct token for a reserved word other than `TRUE` or `FALSE`; for booleans it registers `Subtype.BOOL` and returns `BOOLEAN_LITERAL`; for identifiers it registers initial metadata and returns `IDENTIFIER`. Sources: `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/Identifiers.java`, `src/main/java/lexer/semantics/utils/ReservedWords.java`.

mermaid_diagrams.title:
Purpose

The `utils` package is the shared repository for every compiler phase. It contains the symbol table that stores semantic metadata, the `LexemeInfo` DTO that carries that metadata, the diagnostics collector and diagnostic hierarchy, the builder API used to construct `LexemeInfo`, and the enums that classify symbols.

The package is consumed by the lexer, the parser, the parser publishers and facades, the lowering phase, and the compiler entry point. `utils` itself has no outgoing dependency on another compiler package: it only depends on the JDK, the SpotBugs annotations, and its own `utils.enums` and `utils.diagnostics` subpackages. This page documents `utils` and its subpackages `utils.builders`, `utils.enums`, and `utils.diagnostics`. Helper classes in `parser.utils`, `lexer.semantics.utils`, and `lexer.transformers.utils` belong to the parser and lexer module pages.

sections.Purpose:
The `utils` package is the shared repository for every compiler phase. It contains the symbol table that stores semantic metadata, the `LexemeInfo` DTO that carries that metadata, the diagnostics collector and diagnostic hierarchy, the builder API used to construct `LexemeInfo`, and the enums that classify symbols.

The package is consumed by the lexer, the parser, the parser publishers and facades, the lowering phase, and the compiler entry point. `utils` itself has no outgoing dependency on another compiler package: it only depends on the JDK, the SpotBugs annotations, and its own `utils.enums` and `utils.diagnostics` subpackages. This page documents `utils` and its subpackages `utils.builders`, `utils.enums`, and `utils.diagnostics`. Helper classes in `parser.utils`, `lexer.semantics.utils`, and `lexer.transformers.utils` belong to the parser and lexer module pages.
